scenes.say: Welcome to Sentinel by DeepTrack. In this first video, we'll take a tour of the dashboard, the page you see every time you sign in.
Click Overview at the top of the menu. The Dashboard shows the last thirty days of activity for your organization, here Demo Bank Limited.
At the top is your credit balance. Every check uses credits when it completes. If the balance reaches zero, new checks are rejected, so keep an eye on it.
The four tiles give you the numbers that matter: checks run in the last thirty days, the average time a check takes, how many are flagged and waiting for a person, and your active API keys.
This tile is DeepTrack's deepfake shield. It counts the checks where Sentinel caught a deepfake face or an AI-generated document, out of every check it screened.
Verification mix shows how your work splits by type: identity checks, business checks, documents, AML screening and liveness.
Recent verifications lists your ten latest checks, with each verdict. Approved means it passed. Needs review means a person must decide, in Reviews. Rejected means it failed.
The menu on the left takes you everywhere else. Run identity, business, document and AML checks. Send liveness links. Work cases in Reviews, follow disputes, customer risk and transactions.
Developers find API keys and webhooks at the bottom. And Help is always there, with a chapter for every page you see.
That's the dashboard. Next, we'll see how Sentinel decides whether a check passes, fails or needs a person.
